Not a version of ascot: the pre-built declaration files ascot checks against when no `--iris` is given, one per namespace worth checking against of each Community release of IRIS and of IRIS for Health.

Each `iris-community-<release>.d.json.gz` or `irishealth-community-<release>.d.json.gz` holds the system classes with their members, the include files and the routines of `%SYS`, as the Community image of that release reports them, with the corrections of `src/mask.json` applied; `irishealth-community-<release>.HSLIB.d.json.gz` holds IRIS for Health's `HSLIB`, where its `HS` and `Ens` classes live. `ascot analyze` downloads the one for `--iris <release>` and `--iris-namespace` (the newest IRIS release it knows and `%SYS` by default; `--iris irishealth-community:<release>:HSLIB` for IRIS for Health code) into `~/.ascot` on first use, after checking it against the `.sha256` beside it.

The files are regenerated by the `Declarations` workflow (`scripts/prebuilt-declarations.sh`) and replaced in place, so this release moves while its tag stays.
